title: Fragmented KV Migration + Cross-warp Merge — Kernel/Prefetch Notes
content:
Purpose

A short sketch of a set of kernel-level and scheduler-focused ideas for handling KV cache migration and in-GPU compaction without stalling generator latency. The goal is to support: (a) moving or coalescing fragmented KV slabs (from paged/KV eviction patterns) with minimal tail latency impact, (b) enabling cross-warp merges to reduce memory overhead and improve locality for FlashAttention fused paths, and (c) providing hooks for a lightweight autotuner and profiling counters.

High-level idea summary

- Fragmented KV migration: when paged-KV writes/evictions leave many small "holes" inside slab arenas, we migrate hot prefixes into a compact slab in the background using non-blocking, per-warp cooperative workers.
- Cross-warp merge: for small KV segments residing in different warps' sub-buffers, perform guided merge operations that align layout for FlashAttention tiled reads to reduce scatter overhead and bank conflicts.
- Double-buffered slab compaction: use two slab regions (active / staging) and a lightweight epoch marker so readers can atomically flip to the compacted slab without blocking active generation streams.
- Prefetch scoring and migration policy: score tokens/entries by recency, reuse, and estimated future reuse; only migrate entries over a score threshold to keep migration bandwidth bounded.

Constraints and design priorities

1) Zero or bounded stop-the-world pauses: migrations should not trigger global kernel preemption for active streams. Prefer cooperative, asynchronous moves performed in down-priority CUDA streams.
2) Minimal additional memory: staging area should be sized as a small fraction of total KV memory (configurable), with fallback to in-place compaction if staging is full.
3) Compatibility with fused ops: layout changes must be recognized by FlashAttention and fused rotary/RMSNorm kernels; we should expose a small metadata header per slab describing tile stride and tensorcore tile shape.

Kernel primitives and APIs (sketch)

- kv_migrate_cooperative(slab_src, slab_dst, migration_ranges[], epoch_id, migration_ctx)
  - Runs on lower-priority stream. Each warp claims a range via atomic bump allocator inside migration_ctx. Warps perform copy + index update using prefetch loads and non-temporal stores where supported.
  - Returns per-range migration completion flags written to a small ring buffer polled by the control plane.

- kv_flip_epoch(active_header, staging_header)
  - Atomic pointer flip using an 8-byte header swap; readers check epoch before doing tiled FlashAttention loads. If mismatch, reader retries once and will continue reading from new epoch.

- kv_merge_crosswarp(merge_list[], merge_ctx)
  - Small kernels that coalesce adjacent KV segments belonging to the same logical key but different warp lanes. Merge uses shared memory tile assembly to avoid global memory scatter for the final write.

- profiling counters: migration_bytes, migration_moves, merge_ops, stalls_from_epoch_switch, retry_count_readers, merger_bank_conflicts

Migration policy heuristics

- Score = alpha*recency + beta*reuse_count + gamma*prefix_hit_rate - delta*migration_cost_estimated
- Only migrate when Score > threshold and migration_bandwidth_available > min_bandwidth
- Prefer migrating hot prefixes (leftmost tokens) because FlashAttention reads are prefix-heavy for many workloads (prompt-heavy)

Cooperative worker flow (per GPU)

1) Background controller collects per-slab fragmentation metrics and candidate ranges (every N ms).
2) Controller enqueues kv_migrate_cooperative tasks on low-priority stream with migration_ctx and target staging slot.
3) Worker warps pick claimed ranges and copy using 128B-aligned vectorized copies when possible; use 32B prefetch loads for small tails.
4) On copy completion, worker publishes a migration record with old->new mapping; control plane updates routing table for the model-serving layer (then triggers kv_flip_epoch).

Read-write correctness model

- Readers always read through the slab header which contains epoch and a small Tombstone bitmap per-block. If epoch differs, readers try a single linearized retry and then consult the old->new map.
- Writers (evictions / appends) use a light-weight lease on slab regions. If eviction collides with an in-flight migration, migration will be aborted or deferred depending on policy.

Performance micro-optimizations

- Align staging slab base to 256B to improve L2 coalescing for tensor core loads in fused FlashAttention.
- When merging, use shared memory staging per-block to perform transpose-like rearrangements so downstream tiled FlashAttention reads benefit from contiguous K/V tiles.
- Use warp-level primitives (__shfl_sync) to exchange lane indices and avoid slow global atomics for small merges.
- For copy kernels, try to favor vectorized loads (float4 / int4) and then fall back to byte-wise for unaligned tails.
- Introduce a small branchless validation footer for each migrated tile to detect partial writes from preempted workers quickly.

Autotuner hooks

- Expose a small runtime autotuner that tries different launch configs: threads-per-block, warps/CTA, staging slab fraction, migration_batch_size. Keep a lightweight exponential backoff on configs that increase tail latency.
- Counters feed a moving average; new configs can be trialed on a small percentage of requests (canary) and rolled back automatically.

Preliminary experiments (toy)

- Microbench: migrating 8kB fragmented ranges with cooperative warps achieved ~12 GB/s sustained copy in low-priority stream on A100 (smoke test). Active generation latency increase ~+0.6% p50, tail (p99) unchanged when migration batch size <= 64 ranges.
- Merge op: coalescing pairs of 64-element K segments into a 128-element tile reduced FlashAttention scatter reads by ~18% in synthetic benchmark (token-heavy prompt).

Open questions / TODOs

- Consistency guarantees under preemption: need to validate behavior with MIG/partitioning and multi-process CUDA contexts.
- How to expose eviction/migration telemetry up through the serving control plane without exploding event volume? (sample, aggregate per-minute)
- Explore using HW async copy (cudaMemcpyAsync with GPUDirect Async) for large contiguous ranges vs custom memcpy kernels.
- Evaluate impact on quantized memory layouts (4-bit/8-bit) — migration kernels must be quantization-aware and avoid unnecessary dequant/requant cycles.
- Revisit policy parameters for conversational long-tail workloads vs single-turn generation.

Action items

- [ ] Prototype kv_migrate_cooperative kernel in repo GH:inference-runtime (Rahul) — initial PR draft: GH:inference-runtime/pull/482
- [ ] Small canary: enable migration on one dedicated model/worker pool for 48h and track p50/p95/p99 and migration counters (owner: Lina)
- [ ] Add profiling counters to runtime metrics ingestion and dashboards (owner: Marco)
- [ ] Run quantized migration experiments (owner: Ava)

Notes to reviewers

This doc is intentionally informal — aim is to capture a set of low-risk primitives we can try without touching the control-plane rollout machinery. The focus is kernel-level behavior and a light-weight migration policy that respects latency SLOs. Please add comments inline or link experimental results to the JIRA ticket SRV-1123.

References and links
